SUMMARY: Solid disabled tokens in the ui primitives
USER_STORY: As a user, I want a disabled control to look unavailable rather than broken, and to stay legible.
DESCRIPTION: src/index.css, src/components/ui/button-variants.ts, calendar.tsx, command.tsx, dropdown-menu.tsx, input-group.tsx, input.tsx, label.tsx, select.tsx, switch.tsx, tabs.tsx, textarea.tsx handoff AGENTS.md Section 3, README Part 1 #20. Add a disabled ink and a disabled surface token pair (README: solid #8A8892 for disabled labels, 3.3:1) with dark counterparts chosen to keep at least 3:1 against the dark surface and recorded in index.css with a comment, following the theme-token-contrast pattern. Replace disabled:opacity-*, has-disabled:opacity-*, aria-disabled:opacity-*, data-disabled:opacity-*, peer-disabled and group-data-disabled variants with the tokens plus cursor-not-allowed; the lock glyph is reserved for permission or setup locks (as in the nav), not every control. Buttons: filled variants become the muted surface with the disabled ink, outline and ghost keep their border with the disabled ink. calendar.tsx:131 uses opacity-50 for out-of-month day text; that is not a disabled state, so it stays with an allow-list entry and a reason (see LED-120). Blast radius: button.tsx has graphify degree 43, so every button changes; check Home, Accounts, Budgets, every dialog footer and the Login page in both themes. Add the pair to tests/themeContrast.test.mjs.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) No disabled: or has-disabled: opacity utility remains in src/components/ui; (b) disabled controls use the solid disabled tokens in light and dark and stay at least 3:1 against their surface (test); (c) disabled buttons, inputs, selects, switches, tabs, textareas, labels and command items are visibly distinct from enabled ones without opacity; (d) checked on Home, Accounts, Budgets, the add-transaction dialog and Login at 1280 and 390 in both themes; (e) lint, build and test pass.
